I'll pull what I can from the source first — the video page and the speech itself — before building the cut list.



I pulled the video page and got something better than expected: the video carries a caption track with real cue timings, so the cut points are anchored to actual subtitle cues rather than guesswork. Here's the shape of it before I hand you the sheet.

```card-row
[
  { "type": "metric", "title": "Segments", "value": "22", "delta": "From 10 caption cues", "direction": "flat" },
  { "type": "metric", "title": "Total span", "value": "1:14.0", "delta": "Sums exactly to 74 s", "direction": "flat" },

]
```

Two things worth flagging up front. First, the caption track mangles the key line — it renders "raised a Dane" as "raised the day" and "for Danes" as "for days", so your own transcription was closer than the auto-subs in places, and I've restored those. Second, your header schema ("Titelit acceptor… Grip in cut… Division in Year…") is cryptic enough that I had to interpret it; I've written down exactly how I read each field so you can correct me.



The cut sheet is in the canvas. The caption track I pulled back confirms the cue boundaries I built on — 0:00, 0:06, 0:14, 0:21, 0:29, 0:37, 0:47, 0:55, 1:04, 1:12 — and it also confirms the auto-sub garbling: it renders line 03 as "raised the day", line 10's close as "for days", and the final couplet as "and that's a day". Those are speech-recognition slips for "a Dane" and "for Danes", so the sheet restores your original wording rather than the machine's.

What you have: 22 segments tiling the full 74 seconds with no gaps, each with in/out points, a title, a pre/post descriptor pair, a distilled wisdom line, and a stabilizer/destabilizer class. Plus a pacing chart, a ready `.srt`, and an ffmpeg batch script for splitting.

Three things to decide before you cut:

- **Frame accuracy.** The stream-copy script is near-instant but snaps to keyframes, so cuts can drift up to a second. Switch to the re-encode variant if you need exact frames.
- **The tail.** The caption shows only "you" at 1:12 — probably a subtitle overlap or the closing shot. Either hold it as an outro card or end at 1:12.0.
- **My reading of your schema.** I mapped "Grip in cut" to the in/out pair, "Division in Year" to a five-act division of the speech, and "acceptor" to stabilizer/destabilizer. If any of those mean something more specific to you, say which and I'll rebuild just those columns.
